narrative: Demand for PL2__M0E12B99 is intermittent with a CV of 0.68 and approximately 11% zero-demand days across 237 working-day observations; no statistically significant trend is present. Lead times average 3.83 days with moderate variability (CV=0.32), yielding a sigma-LTD of 282 units and a statistically justified safety stock of 464 units — 43.6% below the current SAP level of 822. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with ROP=1,062 and OQ=445 (EOQ-derived, above MOQ=205) reduces annual inventory costs by 35.4% while fully satisfying the 95% service level and the 2,189-unit storage constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) model is appropriate for this material because demand, while intermittent, occurs on ~89% of working days at volumes that make continuous review practical; the EOQ formula efficiently balances the low ordering cost against holding costs, and a fixed reorder point handles the moderate lead-time variability without requiring a more complex (s,S) or periodic-review structure.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is non-binding at 41.5% utilisation; no capacity-driven order reduction was required. If demand spikes toward the upper tail (>430 units/day) for multiple consecutive days before replenishment, the ROP of 1,062 may be insufficient — a periodic review of the ROP against rolling 30-day demand is recommended.
